taxonomy.note: Species accepted; Texas material belongs to accepted subsp. linearis.

evidence: Kew/POWO accepts Chilopsis linearis and lists Texas within its native range; Kew also accepts subsp. linearis as the Texas subspecies.
Kinney County — a U.S. National Museum boundary survey explicitly records desert willow collected at Fort Clark, Kinney County, in a natural sandy-watercourse context.
Val Verde County — Devils River/Dolan Creek vegetation work in Val Verde County identifies a native desert willow–Roosevelt weed association (Chilopsis linearis–Baccharis neglecta).
USDA Forest Service FEIS and GRIN place the native species/subsp. linearis in western Texas, and TPWD documents it in western/Edwards Plateau riparian systems.
Uvalde County is a supporting occurrence lead, but the available B015 source is not strong enough to count as the required third native county because desert willow is also commonly planted.
target_zone_range.blocking_issue: Two target counties are firm. Broad West Texas/Edwards Plateau statements and local planted occurrences are not converted into a third county under the project rule.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Do not treat modern landscape use in Austin/Hill Country as proof of local nativity. An older NPSOT Boerne article explicitly described desert willow as native west of the Hill Country, while newer NPSOT/TPWD material maps it into Edwards Plateau contexts; this geographic inconsistency is exactly why exact county evidence is required.

morphology.look_here_first: Ignore the flowers first: desert willow is the Bignoniaceae member here that looks like a small willow tree—simple, extremely narrow linear leaves on a woody small tree rather than a climbing vine.
diagnostic_traits: deciduous shrub or small multi-trunk tree rather than a vine
leaves simple, very narrow linear to lanceolate, willow-like, often drooping
leaf attachment can be opposite, subopposite, or alternate depending on shoot
showy fragrant pink/lavender to whitish trumpet-shaped flowers in terminal racemes on new wood
corolla spreads into five ruffled lobes with contrasting throat/nectar guides
fruit a very long slender capsule, commonly 6–10+ inches, persistent into winter
capsule splits to release numerous seeds bearing winged/hairy margins
native habitat strongly associated with dry washes, gravelly streambeds, arroyos, and riparian channels in western Texas

confusers.separator: Black willow can share narrow leaves and riparian habitat, but willow flowers are catkins and fruits are tiny capsules; desert willow has huge trumpet flowers and long bean-like capsules.
Trumpet creeper is a climbing vine with odd-pinnate serrated leaves; desert willow is a tree/shrub with simple linear leaves.
Crossvine is a tendril-climbing vine with two broad leaflets; desert willow is a free-standing tree with narrow simple leaves.
Chitalpa is a cultivated Chilopsis × Catalpa hybrid with broader leaves; do not count landscape chitalpas or cultivars as wild desert willow range evidence.

diagnostic_roles: mature split capsule and winged seeds

installation_guardrail: Do not install as a project-native until the 3-county requirement is met or Calvin explicitly approves a documented exception.
